Fact.Name: Has a prior-year qualified business loss or REIT/PTP loss carryforward
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft line 3: "Qualified business net (loss) carryforward from the prior year"; line 7: "Qualified REIT dividends and qualified PTP (loss) carryforward from the prior year". 26 U.S.C. 199A(c)(2): a negative amount "shall be treated as a loss from a qualified trade or business in the succeeding taxable year". Carryforwards are not modeled, so "yes" is a stop (/flowKnockoutQbiPriorYearCarryforward).

Fact.Name: Is a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft header: "Use this form if your taxable income, before your qualified business income deduction, is at or below $201,750 ($201,775 if married filing separately; $403,500 if married filing jointly), and you aren't a patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative." A patron files Form 8995-A, which is not supported (/flowKnockoutQbiCooperativePatron). 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(7), (g).

Fact.Name: Return has Schedule C qualified business income or loss
Fact.Description: Schedule C net profit or loss is qualified business income or loss: 26 U.S.C. 199A(c)(1), (c)(3). Follows scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss for an unset business list: complete false when the self-employment question is unanswered or "no", true on "yes" (the lines then stay incomplete until the list is filled in).

Fact.Name: Return has qualified business income or loss on Form 8995
Fact.Description: True when /form8995HasScheduleCQbi is true or the filer answered yes to a section 162 Schedule E rental (/scheduleETradeOrBusinessAnsweredYes). 26 U.S.C. 199A(c)(1). An unanswered rental question is complete false on that fact, so a Schedule C return does not go incomplete because Schedule E has not been reached.

Fact.Name: Section 199A threshold amount (Form 8995 limit)
Fact.Description: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.26, PDF pp. 21-22: "For taxable years beginning in 2026, the threshold amounts under § 199A(e)(2) ... are: Married Individuals Filing Joint Returns $403,500 ... Married Individuals Filing Separate Returns $201,775 ... All Other Returns $201,750". Form 8995 (2026) draft header: "at or below $201,750 ($201,775 if married filing separately; $403,500 if married filing jointly)". 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 3: "Your 2026 taxable income before your QBI deduction is less than or equal to $403,500 if married filing jointly, $201,775 if married filing separately, and $201,750 for all other returns". Above it, Form 8995-A applies.

Fact.Name: Section 199A(i) minimum deduction
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(1): the deduction "shall be equal to the greater of— (A) the amount of such deduction determined without regard to this subsection, or (B) $400." Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.12, PDF p. 7: "Section 70105 of the OBBBA amended § 199A(i) to add a minimum deduction of $400 ... The $400 and $1,000 amounts in § 199A(i) will be adjusted for inflation for taxable years beginning after 2026." 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 2: "There is a minimum qualified business income deduction of $400 for taxpayers whose aggregate qualified business income for such taxable year is at least $1,000 with respect to all qualified trades or businesses in which the taxpayer materially participates".

Fact.Name: Section 199A(i) active QBI floor for the minimum deduction
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(A): "a taxpayer whose aggregate qualified business income with respect to all active qualified trades or businesses of the taxpayer for such taxable year is at least $1,000." Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.12, PDF p. 7 (not indexed for 2026).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 2
Fact.Description: Line 2: "Total qualified business income or (loss). Combine lines 1i through 1v, column (c)." Each Schedule C business's QBI is its net profit or loss reduced by the deductible part of self-employment tax: 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 4: "To figure the total amount of QBI, you must consider all items that are attributable to the trade or business. This includes, but isn't limited to, ... deductible part of self-employment tax, self-employment health insurance deduction, and contributions to qualified retirement plans." Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi). The total is scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus scheduleSE /deductibleSelfEmploymentTax (Schedule 1 line 15), the sum of each filer's Schedule SE line 13. Each line 1 column (c) subtracts only that owner's share (/primaryFilerDeductibleSelfEmploymentTax or /secondaryFilerDeductibleSelfEmploymentTax), so the rows still add to line 2. A section 162 rental's line 1(c) is scheduleE /scheduleETradeOrBusinessQbi and is not reduced by self-employment tax (26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(1)). Line 2 adds that amount to the Schedule C component. When Schedule SE line 2 also includes Form 1065 box 14 code A, the deductible part has to be split between the Schedule C trade and the partnership. That split is not computed, so the return stops (/flowKnockoutScheduleCQbiAndK1Box14CodeA). A rental alone does not fire that stop. Schedule 1 lines 16 and 17 are not part of this return.

Fact.Name: Schedule C qualified business income net of deductible self-employment tax
Fact.Description: scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus scheduleSE /deductibleSelfEmploymentTax, rounded to the dollar, when /form8995HasScheduleCQbi is true. $0 otherwise, so a rental-only return does not subtract self-employment tax. Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 3
Fact.Description: Line 3: "Qualified business net (loss) carryforward from the prior year". $0: any carryforward is a stop (/flowKnockoutQbiPriorYearCarryforward).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 4
Fact.Description: Line 4: "Total qualified business income. Combine lines 2 and 3. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 5
Fact.Description: Line 5: "Qualified business income component. Multiply line 4 by 20% (0.20)". 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(2)(A): "20 percent of the taxpayer's qualified business income".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 6
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft line 6: "Qualified REIT dividends and publicly traded partnership (PTP) income or (loss)". 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 5, Line 6: "Enter income as a positive number and losses as a negative number." Determining Your Qualified REIT Dividends, same page: "This amount is reported to you on Form 1099-DIV, line 5." 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A): 20 percent of "the aggregate amount of the qualified REIT dividends and qualified publicly traded partnership income". This line is the sum of 1099-DIV box 5 (dividends /totalSection199ADividends), rounded to whole dollars (26 U.S.C. 6102(a)). No PTP income is included: a PTP stops the return (scheduleE /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIIForeignOrPtp). A supported Part II K-1 has no box 20 code Z or box 17 code V, so it adds nothing here. A box 5 amount that is not a qualified REIT dividend stops (dividends /flowKnockoutSection199ADividendsHoldingPeriod) rather than being omitted.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 7
Fact.Description: Line 7: "Qualified REIT dividends and qualified PTP (loss) carryforward from the prior year". $0: any carryforward is a stop (/flowKnockoutQbiPriorYearCarryforward).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 8
Fact.Description: Line 8: "Total qualified REIT dividends and PTP income. Combine lines 6 and 7. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 9
Fact.Description: Line 9: "REIT and PTP component. Multiply line 8 by 20% (0.20)". 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 10
Fact.Description: Line 10: "Qualified business income deduction before the income limitation. Add lines 5 and 9".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 11
Fact.Description: Line 11: "Taxable income before qualified business income deduction". 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i8995--dft.pdf), PDF p. 6, Line 11: "Form 1040 or 1040-SR filers who file Schedule A: Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a, minus the amounts on Schedule A (Form 1040) lines 4,7,10,15,16, and 17z, and Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 13a." and "Form 1040 or 1040-SR filers who do not file Schedule A: Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a, minus lines 12e, 12f, and 13a." On the 2026 draft Form 1040, 13a is Schedule 1-A line 44. For an itemizer the Schedule A lines here are 4, 7 (5e), 10 and 15, whose sum is scheduleA /scheduleALine18 (the line 18 Yes branch, IRC 68, is the /flowKnockoutScheduleAOverallLimit stop), so the 12e amount equals that sum and 12f is $0. 26 U.S.C. 199A(e)(1): taxable income is "computed ... without regard to any deduction allowable under this section". Not below zero, like Form 1040 line 15.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 12
Fact.Description: Line 12: "Enter your net capital gain, if any, increased by any qualified dividends." 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 6, Line 12: "Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a, plus your net capital gain. If you're not required to file Schedule D (Form 1040), your net capital gain is the amount reported on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a. If you file Schedule D (Form 1040), your net capital gain is the smaller of Schedule D (Form 1040), line 15 or 16, unless line 15 or 16 is zero or less, in which case nothing is added to the qualified dividends." That is the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet line 4 (scheduleD3 /qdcgLine4: line 3a plus the same Schedule D / line 7a amount). 26 U.S.C. 199A(a)(2)(B) and 1(h).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 13
Fact.Description: Line 13: "Subtract line 12 from line 11. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 14
Fact.Description: Line 14: "Income limitation. Multiply line 13 by 20% (0.20)". 26 U.S.C. 199A(a)(2): "an amount equal to 20 percent of the excess (if any) of— (A) the taxable income of the taxpayer for the taxable year, over (B) the net capital gain (as defined in section 1(h))".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 15
Fact.Description: Line 15: "Qualified business income deduction before the minimum deduction for active qualified business income. Enter the smaller of line 10 or line 14". 26 U.S.C. 199A(a): "the lesser of".

Fact.Name: Aggregate QBI from active trades or businesses
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(A): "aggregate qualified business income with respect to all active qualified trades or businesses". When every business and section 162 rental is active this is line 2; when any is not, $0. A return with both active and non-active trades stops (/flowKnockoutQbiMixedParticipation) and this value is not used. Schedule C and Schedule E are counted together (/form8995NonActiveCount).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 16
Fact.Description: Line 16: "Minimum deduction for active qualified business income (see instructions)". 26 U.S.C. 199A(i): $400 (/qbiMinimumDeductionAmount) for an applicable taxpayer, one whose active aggregate QBI is "at least $1,000" (/qbiMinimumActiveQbiAmount); otherwise $0.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 17
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f8995--dft.pdf, PDF p. 2, line 17; Form 1040 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040--dft.pdf, PDF p. 3, line 13b. Line 17: "Qualified business income deduction. Enter the greater of line 15 or line 16. Also enter this amount on the applicable line of your return." That is Form 1040 (2026) draft line 13b (taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction).

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 18
Fact.Description: Line 18: "Total qualified business (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 2 and 3. If greater than zero, enter -0-". Carried to next year under 26 U.S.C. 199A(c)(2). Kept as a negative amount; the form shows it in parentheses.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 19
Fact.Description: Line 19: "Total qualified REIT dividends and PTP (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 6 and 7. If greater than zero, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 1(i) deductible self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Deductible self-employment tax assigned to this row. Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi): the reduction is the part attributable to that trade or business. Each filer's Schedule SE line 13 (/primaryFilerDeductibleSelfEmploymentTax or /secondaryFilerDeductibleSelfEmploymentTax) is split only across that filer's positive-net rows. The row with that filer's largest positive net (the earliest row on a tie) receives the remainder after the other rows of that filer are rounded, so those shares add to that filer's deductible part. A loss row is $0. 26 U.S.C. 6102(a).

Fact.Description: Schedule C businesses with material participation plus section 162 rentals with material participation. 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B), 469(h).

Fact.Name: Count of non-active trades or businesses on Form 8995
Fact.Description: Schedule C businesses without material participation plus section 162 rentals without material participation. Incomplete while either list has an unanswered material-participation question.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 1(i) column (a)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft line 1(i) column (a): trade, business, or aggregation name. Schedule C fills the earlier rows. A later row is the section 162 rental property name. Incomplete when this row has no trade or business, so the PDF field stays blank.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 1(i) column (b)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft line 1(i) column (b). 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, Specific Instructions, Line 1: "Enter on line 1(b) the employer identification number (EIN). If you don't have an EIN, enter your social security number (SSN) or individual taxpayer identification number (ITIN)." The supported Schedule C does not collect an EIN, so this is the owner's TIN. A section 162 rental that is not aggregated uses the filer's SSN or ITIN (/primaryFiler/tin). An EIN is not collected. Column (b) stays blank only when the rental is aggregated. 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 5, Line 1: "If you aggregated multiple trades or businesses into a single business, enter the aggregation group name ... and leave line 1(b) blank."

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 1(i) column (c)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft line 1(i) column (c): qualified business income or (loss). 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 4: the total QBI "includes, but isn't limited to, ... deductible part of self-employment tax". A Schedule C row is that business's net profit or loss minus /form8995Business0SeShare. A section 162 rental row is the property's net income or loss and is not reduced by self-employment tax (26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(1)). Across the rows that exist, column (c) sums to line 2.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 18 amount inside the preprinted parentheses
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft, PDF p. 2, line 18: "Total qualified business (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 2 and 3. If greater than zero, enter -0-". The parentheses are printed on the form. /form8995Line18 is negative or zero; this fact is that amount's absolute value so the field does not also print a minus. Field f1_34[0]. $0 prints because the line says enter -0-.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 line 19 amount inside the preprinted parentheses
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft, PDF p. 2, line 19: "Total qualified REIT dividends and PTP (loss) carryforward. Combine lines 6 and 7. If greater than zero, enter -0-". The parentheses are printed on the form. Field f1_35[0] is that line. Its /TU tooltip still says line 16 and repeats the line 18 caption; the widget is below line 18 and the printed caption is line 19. /form8995Line19 is negative or zero; this fact is the absolute value. $0 prints because the line says enter -0-.

Fact.Name: Form 8995 is filed
Fact.Description: The return has Schedule C qualified business income or loss, a section 162 Schedule E rental (a loss still files Form 8995 to report the line 18 carryforward), or 1099-DIV box 5 is more than $0. 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 5, Line 4: there is no deduction for a qualified business net loss "unless you have qualified REIT dividends or qualified PTP income". 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B). Box 5 with no Schedule C business and no section 162 rental still files the form.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C QBI and Form 1065 box 14 code A
Fact.Description: Treas. Reg. 1.199A-3(b)(1)(vi) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.199A-3): qualified business income is reduced by the deductible part of self-employment tax "attributable to the trade or business." Form 8995 line 2 subtracts the whole deductible part from Schedule C. A nonzero Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A is also on Schedule SE line 2 (26 U.S.C. 1402(a); 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 2), so part of that deduction is attributable to the partnership. The split is not computed. A K-1 with box 14 code A at zero does not change the self-employment tax, and the whole deduction stays attributable to Schedule C. Complete false when there is no Schedule C qualified business income or no nonzero box 14 code A.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 8995 must be attached and there is no MeF mapping
Fact.Description: Form 1040 (2026) draft, PDF p. 3, line 13b: "Qualified business income deduction from Form 8995 or Form 8995-A". Instructions for Form 1040 (2025) draft (the 2026 instructions are not yet posted), PDF p. 35, the QBI line (line 13b on the 2026 form): "Attach whichever form you use (Form 8995 or 8995-A) to your return." 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 6, line 18: "This is the amount to be carried forward to the next year." The 2026 draft Form 8995 is the print template (pdf/2026/IRS8995, #17), so the package can include it, including in a loss year (26 U.S.C. 199A(c)(2)). There is still no MeF mapping, so submitting line 13b would leave Form 8995 off the electronic return. True whenever /form8995Required is true; complete false when it is not required (no Schedule C qualified business income, no section 162 rental, and no 1099-DIV box 5, including when those questions are answered no or not yet answered).

Fact.Name: Knockout: more than five trades or businesses on Form 8995
Fact.Description: 2026 Instructions for Form 8995 draft, PDF p. 5, line 2: "If you have more than five trades or businesses, attach a statement with the name and taxpayer identification number of the trade(s) or business(es) and include the income and loss from those trade(s) or business(es) in the total for line 2." This package does not attach that statement. Column (c) is split only across lines 1(i) through 1(v), so a sixth trade or business would be omitted while line 2 still included it. Schedule C businesses and section 162 rentals are counted together. True when /form8995HasQbi is true and that count is more than five. Complete false when Form 8995 is not required, a list is not finished (that count is 0), or the finished lists together have five or fewer.

Fact.Name: Knockout: taxable income before the QBI deduction is above the Form 8995 threshold (Form 8995-A)
Fact.Description: Form 8995 (2026) draft header: "Use this form if your taxable income, before your qualified business income deduction, is at or below" the threshold (/qbiThresholdAmount). Above it the W-2 wage and UBIA limits and the specified service rules of 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(2)(B), (b)(3) and (d)(3) apply on Form 8995-A, which is not supported. Complete false when Form 8995 is not filed (no Schedule C qualified business income, no section 162 rental, and no 1099-DIV box 5). A box 5 return above the threshold stops even with no Schedule C business and no section 162 rental (#186).

Fact.Name: Knockout: prior-year QBI or REIT/PTP loss carryforward
Fact.Description: Cites on /qbiHasPriorYearLossCarryforward. Form 8995 (2026) draft line 7: "Qualified REIT dividends and qualified PTP (loss) carryforward from the prior year". Complete false when Form 8995 is not filed, or on "no". Incomplete while a filer with Schedule C income, a section 162 rental, or 1099-DIV box 5 has not answered (#186). Line 7 stays $0 on a supported return.

Fact.Name: Knockout: patron of an agricultural or horticultural cooperative (Form 8995-A)
Fact.Description: Cites on /qbiIsCooperativePatron. Complete false without qualified business income or on "no" (#186).

Fact.Name: Knockout: some trades or businesses are active and some are not
Fact.Description: The 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(A) test counts QBI only from trades or businesses with material participation (26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B), 469(h)). Schedule C and section 162 rentals are counted together. A return with both active and non-active trades is stopped. Complete false without qualified business income, when every trade has the same answer, or while a list is unfinished (#186). Incomplete while a listed trade has not answered material participation.

Fact.Name: Show the Form 8995 limit screen for 1099-DIV box 5
Fact.Description: Screen condition only. Not BlockSubmissionOnTrue: the stops themselves are already in /flowIsKnockedOut. True when box 5 is more than $0 and taxable income is above the Form 8995 threshold, a prior-year loss carryforward applies, the filer is a cooperative patron, material participation is mixed, or Schedule C businesses plus section 162 rentals exceed five. /flowKnockoutScheduleCQbi stays false without Schedule C, so this screen is what a box 5 return uses. A section 162 rental with no box 5 does not make this true.
